name: A rota with no double shifts
brief:
A help desk has a bag of shifts, written as a string of initials: `'aab'` means two shifts for `a` and one for `b`. Nobody may work two shifts in a row. Build the rota one slot at a time: each slot goes to the person with the most shifts left, leaving out whoever took the slot before. When two people have equally many shifts left, the one whose initial comes first alphabetically takes the slot.

Return the rota as a string, or `''` when no rota avoids a double shift (an empty bag also gives `''`).

Write `spread_shifts(shifts)`.

Example. For `'aabbcc'` the slots go to `a`, `b`, `c`, then `a`, `b`, `c`, so the answer is `'abcabc'`. For `'ccccd'` no rota works, so the answer is `''`.
constraints: At most $200{,}000$ shifts; initials are lower-case letters.
$O(n \log 26)$ time is the target: a heap of at most 26 people, one push and pop per slot.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep a heap of `(-shifts_left, initial)`. Pop the top; if it took the last slot, pop the next one instead and push the first back. When only the previous person is left, no rota works.

examples.note: Three people tie at two shifts each, so they take turns alphabetically.
Four shifts for `c` need three others between them, and there is only one.
`b` has most, then `a`, then `b` again: the rota is `'babab'`.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Giving each slot to whoever has most left, apart from the last person, never paints the rota into a corner when one exists.
Filling every other slot from the busiest person gives a valid rota, but not the one this rule builds.
Each slot costs a push and a pop on a heap of at most 26, so the work is $O(n \log 26)$.

planted.slip: When only the previous person is left it gives them the slot anyway instead of reporting that no rota works.
Negating the initial to break ties hands a tied slot to the later letter.
Filling the even slots first gives a valid rota, but not the one the slot-by-slot rule builds.
